checks: The centroid is interior to T. The homothet has volume tau V by the dth power scaling. A fixed full-dimensional centrally symmetric body centered at g can be scaled by a positive constant times tau^(1/d) to the same volume and lies in T for all sufficiently small tau. Taking tau≤rho_d/(1+theta) in each case gives both seven-fiber mass conditions. All seven integer sites remain present.

The four core laws are constant and identical. Every added body in both families is supported within O(tau^(1/d)) of g. Uniform continuity near g for bounded continuous test functions gives weak convergence to delta_g on each added fiber.

Since w=a>0 and theta>0, the seven-fiber theorem gives the unique maximizing mark at q. Substitution and division by 4V+3tau V give the two exact ratios. Both extend continuously to Gamma_d/4. Their difference is (1−2 Gamma_d)tau/(4+3tau), so the difference of right derivatives at zero is (1−2 Gamma_d)/4>0. For d=2 the individual derivatives are 7/18 and 5/12, whose difference is 1/36.

For a selected binary vertex v of the padding cube, the affine gap sum over j of v_j(1−z_j)+(1−v_j)z_j is zero at v and at least one at every other binary vertex. Restricting a containing cap to the copy at v gives a containing cap or the whole original space, so its raw mass is at least the original depth. Conversely subtracting M times the gap from the original affine margin, with M larger than its supremum on the compact original source, excludes every other copy strictly and preserves the original trace, including its boundary. This works for arbitrary containing caps and therefore gives pointwise equality after taking infima.

The product is compact and convex and its actual integer sites are exactly the original seven times all binary vertices. Each copy keeps its original fiber volume and law. Total mixed mass is multiplied by 2^(n−2) and every original point has copies, which proves the exact maximum and derivative scaling.
